Reasons
for Judgment of the Honourable Madam Justice Rowles:

[
1
]

Three applications for intervenor status came
before me on 6 June 2002 in two appeals brought from the orders of Mr. Justice
Pitfield dated 2 October 2001 dismissing the appellants’ petitions for
declaratory relief on restrictions placed on the marriage of same sex couples.

[
2
]

In his reasons for judgment, Mr. Justice
Pitfield noted the positions taken in the proceedings by the Attorney General
of Canada and the Attorney General of British Columbia, as well as by the intervenors
in the court below:

[4]  The Attorney
General of Canada, to whom notice of the constitutional question was properly
provided, opposes the petitions saying that the common law does not permit
persons of the same sex to be married and does not infringe any
Charter

right.

[5]  The Attorney
General of Canada is supported by the Interfaith Coalition and the B.C.
Coalition for Family and Marriage who were granted status as intervenors in the
proceeding.

[6]  The Attorney
General of British Columbia endorses the view that, at common law, marriage is
restricted to persons of opposite sex and otherwise takes no position with
respect to the relief claimed in the petitions.

[
3
]

When the application was heard, I granted
intervenor status to the B.C Coalition for Marriage and Family and the
Interfaith Coalition for Marriage, both of whom had been intervenors in the
court below, and gave certain directions in that regard pursuant to s. 35 of
the
Rules of Court
.

[
4
]

The third application was brought by the
Coalition of Canadian Liberal Rabbis for Same-Sex Marriage (the “Coalition”).
The Attorney General for British Columbia took no position on the Coalition’s
application but the Attorney General for Canada opposed it, submitting that the
Coalition’s application did not meet the criteria established under the case
law for granting intervenor status.

[
5
]

Counsel were subsequently informed through the
Court of Appeal Registry that the Coalition’s application for leave to
intervene was granted with reasons to follow.  These are my reasons for
concluding that the application of the Coalition, which consists of

a

group

of

Canadian
Reform, Reconstructionist and Jewish Renewal rabbis, ought to be granted
intervenor status.

[
6
]

The principles to be applied on applications for
intervenor status have been considered by this Court in a number of cases
including
Guadagni v. British Columbia (Workers’ Compensation Board)

(1988),
1988 CanLII 3134 (BC CA)
, 30 B.C.L.R. (2d) 259 (C.A.) (Locke J.A. in chambers);
Canada
(Attorney General) v. Aluminium Co. of Canada Ltd.
(1987),
1987 CanLII 162 (BC CA)
, 10 B.C.L.R.
(2d) 371, 15 C.P.C. (2d) 289 (C.A.);
MacMillan Bloedel Ltd. v. Mullin

(1985),
1985 CanLII 152 (BC CA)
, 66 B.C.L.R. 207 (C.A.) (Esson J.A. in chambers);
Bosa Development
Corp. v. British Columbia (Assessor of Area 12 – Coquitlam)

(1996), 82
B.C.A.C. 260 (Williams J.A. in chambers)
;
Hobbs v. Robertson
,
[2002] B.C.J. No. 454 (Q.L.),
2002 BCCA 168 (Esson J.A. in chambers)
; and
Ward
v. Clark
, [2001] B.C.J. No. 901 (Q.L.),
2001 BCCA 264
.

[
7
]

Generally speaking, before an applicant will be
allowed to intervene, the court should consider whether the applicant has a
direct interest in the litigation or whether the applicant can make a valuable
contribution or bring a different perspective to a consideration of the issues
that differs from those of the parties.  When an application for intervention
is made on a public law issue, the application may be allowed even though the
applicant does not have a direct interest in the appeal.

[
8
]

In this case, the applicant consists of a group
of liberal rabbis from across Canada who believe that same-sex couples should
be able to choose to have a civil marriage ceremony and that religious groups
should be able to choose whether they will hold a marriage ceremony for
same-sex couples.

[
9
]

The Coalition is committed to greater inclusion
of gays and lesbians in their religious and cultural life and support civil
equality for gays and lesbians and oppressed minorities as a priority for
social action.

[
10
]

As to the Coalition’s interest in the litigation, the Coalition
states as part of its written submissions on the application:

5.   We believe our right to freedom of
conscience and religion pursuant to Section 2(a) of the
Charter of Rights
and Freedoms
and our right to the equal protection and equal benefit of the
law pursuant to Section 15(1) of the
Charter of Rights and Freedoms
is
affected by this litigation because:

a)   We support the right of Jewish same-sex couples to celebrate
religious same-sex marriage ceremonies duly recognized in Canadian law;

b)   We support the right of interfaith and non-Jewish same-sex
couples to obtain binding civil same-sex marriages duly recognized in Canadian
law;

c)   We support the right of rabbis and their congregations to
celebrate a marriage between a same-couple, if they so choose;

d)   We support the
right of interfaith and non-Jewish same-sex couples to obtain binding civil
same-sex marriages duly recognized in Canadian law.

[
11
]

The Coalition wishes to put forward the perspective of a number of
Canadian rabbis who recognize that, as in other religions, there are divergent
positions that are legitimately held within Judaism on the issue of the
extension of civil same-sex marriage but who would caution against the
absolutist positions of some conservative or traditional groups within a
particular faith or within a coalition of fundamentalist religious views across
faiths.

[
12
]

The Coalition will submit that religious and cultural diversity and
freedoms in Canada would not be threatened by allowing same-sex marriage,
religious or civil, and that the provision of same-sex marriage in religious
contexts demonstrates the concerted commitment of members of the gay and
lesbian communities to form families and to contribute to the stability and
well-being of their communities.

[
13
]

I am persuaded that the Coalition is able to put forward a perspective
that differs from the parties and other intervenors and may be of assistance to
the court in considering the arguments under the
Charter
.

[
14
]

The application of the Coalition of Canadian Liberal Rabbis for
Same-Sex Marriage is granted.  The same directions that were given with respect
to the other intervenors will apply to this intervenor.

"THE HONOURABLE MADAM JUSTICE ROWLES"
